pharm: Antineoplastic - hormonal therapy for prostate cancer
quick: 50 mg orally once daily with an LHRH analog
Take with or without food, at the same time each day
Contraindicated / not indicated in women - can cause fetal harm
No adjustment for mild-moderate; caution in severe (longer half-life)
Serum transaminases, PSA, INR if on warfarin, blood glucose
summary: Bicalutamide is a non-steroidal androgen-receptor antagonist used at 50 mg once daily in combination with an LHRH analog for Stage D2 metastatic prostate cancer. It competitively blocks androgen binding at the receptor in prostate tissue. The 150 mg dose and monotherapy are not FDA-approved. Key safety issues are severe (occasionally fatal) hepatotoxicity - monitor transaminases especially in the first four months - potentiation of warfarin (monitor INR), gynecomastia, and reduced glucose tolerance when combined with LHRH agonists. It is contraindicated in women and pregnancy.
indications: Treatment of Stage D2 metastatic carcinoma of the prostate, in combination with a luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) analog

dosage.d: 50 mg once daily with an LHRH analog
dosage.n: Start at the same time as the LHRH analog; same time each day

admin: Take one 50 mg tablet once daily, morning or evening, with or without food
Take at the same time each day and start concurrently with the LHRH analog
Do not interrupt or stop either drug without consulting the prescriber
Measure serum transaminases at baseline, regularly for the first 4 months, then periodically
If on warfarin, monitor PT/INR closely and adjust anticoagulant dose
moa: Bicalutamide is a non-steroidal androgen-receptor inhibitor that competitively binds cytosolic androgen receptors in target tissue, blocking the action of androgens. Prostate carcinoma is androgen-sensitive, so combined with the testosterone suppression produced by an LHRH analog, bicalutamide provides complete androgen blockade. It does not affect LHRH-analog-induced testosterone suppression.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to bicalutamide or any component (angioedema, urticaria reported)
relative: Diabetes / impaired glucose tolerance (with LHRH agonist)
monitor: Serum transaminases (baseline, first 4 months, then periodic)

preg: Contraindicated and not indicated in females. Bicalutamide can cause fetal harm; animal studies show feminization and abnormal reproductive-organ development in male offspring. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during and for 130 days after the final dose.
lact: Not indicated for use in women, so lactation is not applicable; it should not be used by breastfeeding women.
renal: No dosage adjustment is necessary in renal impairment.
hepatic: No adjustment for mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment. In severe impairment the half-life of the active R-enantiomer is prolonged (~76% increase); although no formal adjustment is specified, use with caution and monitor for hepatotoxicity.

major: Coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin) - bicalutamide displaces them from protein binding and may raise INR/bleeding risk; monitor PT/INR closely
CYP3A4 substrates with narrow index (e.g., midazolam) - R-bicalutamide inhibits CYP3A4, raising their levels
moderate: LHRH agonists - reduced glucose tolerance; monitor blood glucose
Other CYP2C9/2C19/2D6 substrates - possible modest inhibition
minor: No clinically significant interaction with goserelin or leuprolide pharmacokinetics
interactions.food: No clinically significant effect of food on absorption.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; moderate intake is acceptable.
interactions.diagnostics: Can raise serum transaminases; may increase INR with warfarin; combined with LHRH agonists may raise blood glucose; PSA is followed for response.

serious: Severe hepatic injury / fatal hepatic failure
Reduced glucose tolerance / hyperglycemia (with LHRH agonist)
emergency: Signs of hepatic failure (jaundice, dark urine, severe fatigue, RUQ pain)

monitoring: Serum transaminases at baseline, regularly for the first four months, then periodically and with any hepatic symptoms
PSA to assess response (evaluate for progression if PSA rises)
PT/INR in patients on coumarin anticoagulants
Blood glucose in patients on combined LHRH-agonist therapy
counsel: Take it at the same time each day and start it together with your LHRH injection; do not stop either without asking your doctor
Hot flashes and some breast tenderness/enlargement are common
Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, nausea or stomach pain - your liver will be checked
If you take a blood thinner (warfarin), tell your doctor - your clotting tests will be monitored
Avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen; report any new breathing problems
pk: Gradual androgen blockade; PSA decline over weeks
Time to peak of active R-enantiomer ~31 hours
~5.8 days (active R-enantiomer); ~10.4 days in severe hepatic impairment
pearls: FDA-approved only at 50 mg with an LHRH analog for Stage D2 disease; 150 mg and monotherapy are not approved
Severe, sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity - check LFTs at baseline, frequently for 4 months, then periodically
Potentiates warfarin by protein-binding displacement - monitor INR
Inhibits CYP3A4 - caution with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates (e.g., midazolam)
Contraindicated in women and pregnancy; advise male contraception for 130 days after the last dose
missed: If a dose is missed, take the next dose at its scheduled time. Do not take the missed dose and do not double the next dose.
overdose: No specific antidote; treatment is symptomatic and supportive. Doses up to 200 mg/day have been well tolerated and no single life-threatening overdose dose is established. Induce vomiting only if the patient is alert; provide supportive care with monitoring of vital signs. Dialysis is unlikely to help because bicalutamide is highly protein bound and extensively metabolized.
